data.gender_notes: Parshu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Parshu is the name of the divine ax wielded by Lord Shiva, the god of destruction. The name is derived from the Sanskrit word 'parsha', meaning 'to divide'. Parshu represents strength, power, and destruction, and is often used as a symbol of transformation and renewal in Hinduism. The name Parshu carries the meaning “Ax wielder, warrior” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Parshu usually hope their child will grow to embody ax wielder, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Parshu represents the divine power and strength within us, and the ability to destroy negative influences and obstacles in our lives. It is a reminder to use our power wisely and for the greater good, and to remain grounded and focused in the face of challenges.
data.etymology: Parshu belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ax wielder, warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Parshu total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
